didntUnderstand.item: Not understood: 'Similar checks' (step 2 in the progress list). I never learned what it checks against what.
Not understood: 'Questions' (step 4) versus 'Your answers' (step 3). I thought I was answering questions at step 3 already, so I can't tell what step 4 adds.
Not understood: 'Someone who runs Ollama can connect an AI model under Settings' and 'Setup steps for whoever runs Ollama'. I don't know what Ollama is or who in my firm runs it.

Not understood: 'alpha:7b' and 'AI helper alpha:7b: not yet tested on the example cases'. I don't know what alpha:7b is, why it matters that it is 'not yet tested', or whether I should trust its suggestions.

Unclear: 'Where does the AI come from?' has overlapping options. My service is 'approved cloud LLM service'. 'An AI assistant or website run by an outside company — including company accounts your firm set up' and 'Your firm's cloud AI assistant' could both fit. I picked the second but I'm not sure it's right.
Unclear: 'Which countries does it involve?' My packet didn't say where my branch is, so I picked 'Somewhere else, or not sure'. I'm not sure that is a good answer.

Slightly unclear: on the first screen, 'We found no words about: Where does the AI come from' and 'Who ends up receiving what it produces' puzzled me, because I wrote 'approved cloud LLM service' and 'customer questions'. I wasn't sure what counts as 'words found'.

Slightly unclear: 'What it can get into by itself' in the 'We found no words about' list. It seems to mean what systems the tool can reach, and the example helped a little, but it doesn't apply to my chatbot.

expectNext: On the first screen I would just press Next again, because I don't want to add anything. I think the form then lets me fix any answers I disagree with. When I press Continue I expect to reach a 'Questions' step with possibly a few more questions, then a 'Confirm' step where I check everything, and finally a 'Result' telling me whether I can go ahead with the chatbot and what has to be done first. I expect that result to come from my firm's written rules and not from the AI, and that the same answers would always give the same result.
ticksMean: Ticking 'I've checked this answer' means I have read the AI helper's suggestion, compared it with what I actually meant, and agree it is correct. The suggestion doesn't count until I tick it or change it, and I can't press Continue until every suggestion has one or the other. So the tick is my own confirmation and not the AI's decision.
comment: As a branch lead I would have ticked the other two suggestions but changed the middle one, because a chatbot that only drafts replies for a person to send is not the same as one that answers customers directly.
